async def act(page):
    import re
    import asyncio

    # Navigate to the Orders grid using a relative URL from the current admin dashboard
    await page.goto("/index.php/admin/sales_order/index/")
    await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
    # small extra wait to allow dynamic grid content to render
    await asyncio.sleep(1)

    # Locate rows that mention "fraud" (case-insensitive)
    fraud_rows = page.get_by_role("row").filter(has_text=re.compile(r"fraud", re.I))
    count = await fraud_rows.count()
    if count == 0:
        # No fraud-suspect orders found -> print empty string
        print("")
        return

    # Assume grid lists newest first; earliest matching fraud order is the last match
    target_row = fraud_rows.nth(count - 1)

    # Heuristic pattern for capitalized multi-word names
    name_re = re.compile(r"^[A-Z][A-Za-z'`.-]+(?: [A-Z][A-Za-z'`.-]+)+$")

    def looks_like_name(s: str) -> bool:
        s = s.strip()
        if not s or len(s) < 3:
            return False
        # Exclude obvious non-name tokens
        if "$" in s or "#" in s:
            return False
        if re.search(r"\d{4,}", s):
            return False
        if re.search(r"\b(?:fraud|fraudulent|review|pending|processing|complete|closed|canceled)\b", s, re.I):
            return False
        if name_re.match(s):
            return True
        if " " in s and re.search(r"[A-Za-z]", s):
            return True
        return False

    customer_name = ""

    # Inspect cells in the target row first
    cells = target_row.get_by_role("cell")
    try:
        cells_count = await cells.count()
    except Exception:
        cells_count = 0

    for i in range(cells_count):
        text = (await cells.nth(i).inner_text()).strip()
        if looks_like_name(text):
            customer_name = text
            break

    # Fallback: parse the full row inner text into chunks and pick the best candidate
    if not customer_name:
        full_text = (await target_row.inner_text()).strip()
        candidates = [c.strip() for c in re.split(r"\s{2,}|\n", full_text) if c.strip()]
        for c in candidates:
            if looks_like_name(c):
                customer_name = c
                break
        if not customer_name:
            for c in candidates:
                if " " in c and re.search(r"[A-Za-z]", c) and not re.search(r"\$|#|\d{4,}", c):
                    customer_name = c
                    break
        if not customer_name and candidates:
            customer_name = candidates[0]

    # Print only the customer name (or empty string if none found)
    print(customer_name)
